title: Maximum White Tiles Covered by a Carpet
summary: Given a range of white tiles and a carpet length, determine the maximum number of white tiles that can be covered by placing the carpet anywhere.
statement: Given a range of white tiles and a carpet length, determine the maximum number of white tiles that can be covered by placing the carpet anywhere.
constraints: Each inclusive interval [left,right] contains white tiles and intervals do not overlap.
A carpet covers carpet_len consecutive integer positions and may start anywhere.
Return the greatest number of white tiles covered, including partial boundary intervals.
hints: Sort intervals and align a candidate carpet’s right edge with each interval end.
Maintain total white length of intervals intersecting that carpet and remove intervals wholly left of it.
Subtract only the uncovered prefix of the current leftmost interval before updating the answer.
Sliding endpoints visit every structurally optimal right alignment, and the correction gives the exact covered portion of the sole partial interval.
editorial: Sliding endpoints visit every structurally optimal right alignment, and the correction gives the exact covered portion of the sole partial interval.

tests.explanation: A best length-ten placement covers nine white positions across neighboring intervals.
A length-two carpet can cover both tiles in interval [10,11].
